--- a/roaring_test.go
+++ b/roaring_test.go
@@ -3376,3 +3376,49 @@ func TestValidateFromV1(t *testing.T) {
 	require.NoError(t, v2.UnmarshalBinary(b))
 	require.NoError(t, v2.Validate())
 }
+
+func TestCheckedAdd(t *testing.T) {
+	rb := NewBitmap()
+	
+	// Adding a new element should return true
+	added := rb.CheckedAdd(100)
+	assert.True(t, added, "First addition should return true")
+	
+	// Adding the same element again should return false
+	added = rb.CheckedAdd(100)
+	assert.False(t, added, "Adding existing element should return false")
+	
+	// Adding another new element should return true
+	added = rb.CheckedAdd(200)
+	assert.True(t, added, "Adding another new element should return true")
+	
+	// Verify the elements are actually in the bitmap
+	assert.True(t, rb.Contains(100), "Bitmap should contain 100")
+	assert.True(t, rb.Contains(200), "Bitmap should contain 200")
+	assert.False(t, rb.Contains(150), "Bitmap should not contain 150")
+}
+
+func TestCheckedRemove(t *testing.T) {
+	rb := NewBitmap()
+	rb.Add(100)
+	rb.Add(200)
+	
+	// Removing an existing element should return true
+	removed := rb.CheckedRemove(100)
+	assert.True(t, removed, "Removing existing element should return true")
+	
+	// Removing the same element again should return false
+	removed = rb.CheckedRemove(100)
+	assert.False(t, removed, "Removing non-existing element should return false")
+	
+	// Verify the element was actually removed
+	assert.False(t, rb.Contains(100), "Bitmap should not contain 100 after removal")
+	assert.True(t, rb.Contains(200), "Bitmap should still contain 200")
+	
+	// Removing another existing element should return true
+	removed = rb.CheckedRemove(200)
+	assert.True(t, removed, "Removing another existing element should return true")
+	
+	// Verify the bitmap is now empty
+	assert.Equal(t, uint64(0), rb.GetCardinality(), "Bitmap should be empty")
+}

// Package roaring is an implementation of Roaring Bitmaps in Go.
// They provide fast compressed bitmap data structures (also called bitset).
// They are ideally suited to represent sets of integers over
// relatively small ranges.
// See http://roaringbitmap.org for details.
package roaring

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/base64"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"strconv"

	"github.com/RoaringBitmap/roaring/v2/internal"
	"github.com/bits-and-blooms/bitset"
)

// Bitmap represents a compressed bitmap where you can add integers.
type Bitmap struct {
	highlowcontainer roaringArray
}

// ToBase64 serializes a bitmap as Base64
func (rb *Bitmap) ToBase64() (string, error) {
	buf := new(bytes.Buffer)
	_, err := rb.WriteTo(buf)
	return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(buf.Bytes()), err
}

// FromBase64 deserializes a bitmap from Base64
func (rb *Bitmap) FromBase64(str string) (int64, error) {
	data, err := base64.StdEncoding.DecodeString(str)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	buf := bytes.NewBuffer(data)

	return rb.ReadFrom(buf)
}

// WriteTo writes a serialized version of this bitmap to stream.
// The format is compatible with other RoaringBitmap
// implementations (Java, C) and is documented here:
// https://github.com/RoaringBitmap/RoaringFormatSpec
func (rb *Bitmap) WriteTo(stream io.Writer) (int64, error) {
	return rb.highlowcontainer.writeTo(stream)
}
